newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL SHARES END UP ON LOCAL FUNDS SUPPORT, OFF HIGHS.
newsitem.headline: KL SHARES END UP ON LOCAL FUNDS SUPPORT, OFF HIGHS.

text.p: Malaysian shares ended higher on Friday as local institutions heeded Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad's advice to start buying since weeks of incessant selling had lowerd their values, dealers and analysts said.
The key Composite Index closed 4.03 points, 0.43 percent, higher at 932.36, after peaking at 942.25 earlier in the day.
"It's true, local funds have been seen supporting the index after PM's statement yesterday," said Soh Meng Hui, research manager at KL City Securities.
Blue chips Genting and Tenaga gained 10 and 20 cents respectively.
"I expect local funds to come in. If I were a player, I would come in and buy," Mahathir told reporters on Thursday when asked about the prospects for the local stock market.
Genting rose inspite of posting a two-percent fall in net earnings for the six months to June 30, 1997. Analysts said the lower profits had already been factored into the price.
Debutante Utama Banking closed at 3.12, just above its offer price of 3.00 ringgit. Analysts said the weak performance was due to the general cautiousness in the market.
Volume stood at 259 million shares valued at 1,394 million ringgit. Losers outpaced gainers 333 to 275.
National car distributor Edaran Otomobil Nasional (EON) fell 1.80 ringgit to 16.60 ringgit, hitting a new low of 16.30 for 1997.
Projected slower earnings at associate car maker Proton, the possible sale of its banking unit and recent interest rate increases were possible explanations for the fall, said analysts.

On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange the spot August contract lost 0.5 of a point to 926.0 with 1,400 lots traded. September futures shed 4.0 points to 929.0, with four lots having changed hands.
